title: Reserve Fleet micro-cockpit with SLA heatmap and policy composer
creator: Riley Chen
description: Design a compact, high-density micro-cockpit for Dedicated GPU fleets that surfaces fleet health and provides lightweight controls for autoscaling and burst behavior. The screen combines an SLA heatmap (latency & error percentiles across pools), a KV-cache and GPU utilization strip, a burst-budget slider with real-time cost estimate, and an autoscale policy composer for common patterns (CPU/GPU utilization, queued requests, latency SLO breaches). The UI must support on-call quick actions (drain, put-in-maintenance, force-burst), be usable at a glance in pager contexts, and degrade gracefully to a compact telemetry-only mode. Prototypes should cover desktop and tablet widths and include accessible color choices for heatmap gradients.
acceptance_criteria: Heatmap shows 1m/5m/95th latency percentiles per pool and can be toggled to show errors or SLO breach rate
Burst budget slider adjusts numeric burst capacity and displays an estimated hourly cost delta inline
Autoscale policy composer supports at least three templates (steady-throughput, latency-surge, queue-backed) and allows threshold editing with preview of expected scaling behavior
Quick actions (drain, maintenance, force-burst) are visible and require confirmation modals; actions post to staging API endpoints documented in attachments
Design spec includes Figma prototype links, component tokens, and accessibility contrast checks
Engineering has sign-off on layout responsiveness and data requirements (metrics endpoints and rate limits)
design_notes: Use a compact 3-column layout: left (controls + quick actions), center (heatmap + time scrubber), right (detailed metrics + policy composer preview)
Heatmap color scale must be colorblind-friendly; prefer blue->orange diverging palette with pattern overlay on critical cells for additional redundancy
Burst slider should be continuous with step presets (x1, x2, x4) and show instantaneous projected TPS and cost; consider debounce before apply
Policy composer will present templates first; advanced mode exposes JSON editor tied to schema validation
Micro-interactions: hover cell reveals last 3 spikes, click opens timeline; applying burst shows an animated token debit indicator
Density mode for pager: hide explanatory copy and increase glyph sizes for visibility on secondary monitors
decisions: Chosen compact micro-cockpit over full dashboard to optimize for on-call usage and reduce navigation friction
Expose both templated autoscale policies and an advanced JSON editor to balance discoverability and flexibility
Use server-provided aggregated metrics (1m/5m windows) to limit frontend compute and bandwidth
Cost estimates for burst will be calculated client-side using a concise pricing model endpoint; final billing remains server-side
blockers: Missing metrics endpoint for burst_budget and kv_cache_hit_rate (ENG dependency)
Backend rate-limiting behavior unknown for heatmap scrubbing; needs infra clarification
Telemetry sampling changes planned for runtime-1.20 may alter payload shapes
Need engineering capacity for integration tests before design handoff
